title: Alignment: Jansenists and recent Thomists with the Dort Reformed; Remonstrants with the Molinists
source_text: XXXVI. Ac praeterea sicut hac in parte communibus armis Molinistas impugnant cum Reformatis illis qui Dordracenae Synodo subscribunt, nonnulli Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, ut qui vocantur Jansenistae, & Thomistae illi quoque recentiores: sic a parte Molinistarum stant, & eorum in hac quaestione doctrinam acerrime defendunt illi ex Reformatis qui in Belgio dicuntur Remonstrantes sive Arminiani, aliique qui Dordracenam Synodum non sequuntur.
pass_a_gloss: And moreover as in this part some Doctors of the Roman Church, as those who are called Jansenists, and those more recent Thomists also, attack the Molinists with common arms with those Reformed who subscribe to the Synod of Dort: so on the side of the Molinists stand, and most sharply defend their doctrine in this question, those of the Reformed who in the Netherlands are called Remonstrants or Arminians, and others who do not follow the Synod of Dort.
pass_b_english: On this point, moreover, some teachers of the Roman Church, namely the so-called Jansenists and those more recent Thomists as well, join forces against the Molinists with the Reformed who subscribe to the Synod of Dort.

On the Molinists' side, by contrast, stand those Reformed in the Netherlands called Remonstrants or Arminians, along with others who do not follow the Synod of Dort, and they defend the Molinist teaching on this question very vigorously.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
